strengths: Comprehensive experimental design with controlled comparison of three propagators within the same fixed latent space, isolating the effect of propagation mechanisms
Exemplary reproducibility with detailed algorithms, extensive hyperparameter tables, and promised code release; sets high standard for reproducible research
Multi-faceted evaluation framework combining multiple complementary metrics (JSD, TICA timescales, IDDT, contact correlations, free-energy surfaces) appropriate for the problem
Extensive ablation studies investigating encoder width, pooling dimensions, denoiser settings, data efficiency, and architectural choices demonstrate scientific rigor

Actionable practical insights about different propagators: autoregressive NN most robust for long-horizon simulations, score-guided Langevin best for side-chain dynamics, Koopman as lightweight baseline
Demonstrated functional relevance through recovery of A₂AR GPCR activation surface with correct transition pathway
Testing on systems up to 370 residues with 100,000-frame simulations demonstrates practical scalability
Well-motivated approach addressing critical challenge of long-timescale protein dynamics simulation
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: individual components (LD-FPG, Koopman, score-guided diffusion, autoregressive NNs) are well-established; contribution is primarily in application and controlled comparison rather than fundamental innovation

Frozen encoder-decoder constrains the approach: prevents end-to-end optimization for dynamics and lacks theoretical/empirical justification that LD-FPG's latent space is optimal for dynamics simulation
Insufficient analysis of latent space quality: no quantification of how encoder/decoder errors propagate to propagator errors, unclear if pooling operation preserves dynamically relevant information

Theoretical gaps: score-guided Langevin assumes accurate scores but learned denoiser provides only approximations; 'unperturbed score' at τ=0 is heuristic; no rigorous justification why structure-generation latent space captures dynamics

Evaluation limitations: baseline comparisons use different encoders (not fully controlled), Langevin failure analysis is post-hoc rather than principled, 'frame' calibration introduces confounds, missing comparisons to recent methods (AlphaFold dynamics, E(n)-equivariant models)
Insufficient computational cost analysis: wall-clock speedups vs. standard MD unclear, GPU memory requirements not discussed, practical utility for drug discovery not demonstrated
Limited scope: all systems <400 residues, no cross-protein generalization studied, no validation against experimental dynamics (NMR, cryo-EM), equilibrium assumption may not hold
Hyperparameter selection appears empirically driven rather than principled; system-specific tuning raises questions about robustness and transferability
Missing end-to-end training experiments and validation against real biological targets or drug discovery benchmarks
Incomplete theoretical understanding: Koopman linearization assumed but not validated, kinetic validation on generated trajectories limited to Figure 2

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across systems of increasing complexity with appropriate evaluation metrics (JSD, TICA timescales, contact correlations, kinetic fidelity)
Systematic comparison of three propagation mechanisms within a single latent space enabling controlled ablation of propagator effects
Excellent reproducibility with detailed appendices, hyperparameters, algorithms, and explicit code/data availability statements
Functional validation on GPCR activation surfaces (A2AR, A1AR) demonstrating relevance beyond structural metrics
Long-horizon rollout stability analysis (10,000 frames) providing thorough assessment of method robustness
weaknesses: Limited core novelty: all three propagators (Koopman, autoregressive NN, score-guided Langevin) are existing techniques applied within a fixed latent space, appearing incremental over existing latent space simulators (LSS, MD-Gen, GeoTDM)
Frozen encoder-decoder is insufficiently justified and severely constrains potential; no exploration of jointly training encoder + propagator which could substantially improve performance

Unfair baseline comparisons: baselines evaluated on their own learned representations while GLDP uses LD-FPG space, making it unclear whether advantages come from better propagators or superior latent space quality

Marginal improvements over baselines that are metric/system-dependent (e.g., GeoTDM achieves 0.633 contact correlation on ADP vs GLDP's 0.459); claims of superiority often appear selective rather than comprehensive
Superficial analysis of Langevin failure (Section 4.2) that identifies symptoms but not root causes of why score-guided methods struggle in learned spaces
Limited system diversity (only small-to-medium proteins up to ~1000 atoms) with no demonstrations on large complexes; scalability undemonstrated

TICA timescale validation is circular: matching ground truth timescales isn't surprising when slow modes are learned from reference data; genuine kinetic validation (transition paths, rate constants) needed

Missing critical ablations: no training on random latent spaces to isolate LD-FPG representation quality, no sensitivity analysis to encoder/decoder choices, limited exploration of latent space properties
Generalization not demonstrated: all training uses fixed-forcefield MD with no out-of-distribution tests (different temperatures, forcefields, conditions)
Confusing 'frame' definitions across propagators (Langevin's 'frame' = sampled SDE state, not integrator step) that muddle fair comparison and reproducibility

strengths: Rigorous experimental design with controlled comparison: fixes encoder-decoder, swaps only propagators, isolating propagator effects
Comprehensive evaluation across systems of increasing complexity (ADP, 7IFL, 1R6W, GPCRs) with diverse metrics (JSD, TICA, contact maps, free-energy surfaces)
Novel methodology: score-guided Langevin propagation in latent space creatively combines physical guidance with neural encodings
Strong empirical results: GLDP achieves lowest JSD on complex systems (A₁AR backbone 0.019 vs baselines 0.043-0.134) and captures kinetic timescales accurately
Excellent reproducibility: promises code release, provides detailed hyperparameters (Tables 3-9), clear algorithms, and systematic ablation studies (d_z, H, Langevin settings, frame skipping)
Thorough kinetic analysis: TICA-based approach with practical 'failure time' metrics provides credible kinetic fidelity assessment beyond standard structure metrics
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (workflow overview, functional free-energy surfaces, Ramachandran/side-chain comparisons)
Acknowledges method-specific failure modes rather than hiding limitations (e.g., Langevin failure on alanine dipeptide due to rough score estimates)
weaknesses: Limited architectural novelty: LD-FPG backbone is pre-trained and frozen; main contribution is comparing propagators rather than introducing fundamentally new methods
Generalization to new systems not demonstrated: all results use same pre-trained encoder; no transfer learning or fine-tuning experiments on held-out proteins
Incomplete computational cost-benefit analysis: no comparison of total cost (LD-FPG training + GLDP vs native MD); encoder/decoder overhead not quantified; missing coarse-grained MD comparisons

Limited system diversity: four systems tested, mostly small well-characterized proteins; absent are large multi-domain proteins, intrinsically disordered regions, or systems with weak force field coverage

Score-guided Langevin requires heavy per-system calibration: temperature T, step size Δt, diffusion schedule, and denoiser training differ per system (Table 9), raising practical usability and transferability concerns
Inconsistent performance across methods: Langevin fails on alanine dipeptide but excels on GPCRs; underlying reasons for method-system compatibility remain unclear, limiting predictability
Statistical rigor issues: means ± SD over 5 runs with some modest differences (0.052 vs 0.053); no statistical significance testing or confidence intervals; multiple comparisons lack correction

Incomplete baseline comparisons: MD-Gen and GeoTDM comparisons limited (GeoTDM exceeds memory on some systems); missing comparisons with other Koopman-based dynamics methods; no quantitative comparison with simple native MD ensembles

Free-energy surface evaluation qualitative: Section 4.4 relies on visual inspection of activation pathways; lacks quantitative metrics for FES accuracy (RMSE, barrier heights, transition state positioning)

Data efficiency analysis incomplete: Table 10 shows sharp threshold at 25% data but doesn't compare to training baselines from scratch; unclear if latent-space approach is more data-efficient than native MD

Temporal coherence limited to local metrics: TICA and IDDT measure local consistency but miss long-term physical realism (energy conservation, secondary structure stability over 10k+ frames, motif persistence)
Practical deployment pipeline unclear: no decision rules for selecting propagators on new systems, no guidance on hyperparameter selection, startup cost of encoding not quantified
Title framing "Beyond Ensembles" somewhat misleading: unclear what ensemble-related problem is solved; advantage over N independent short MD trajectories not quantified
